title: Bilirubin Blood Test
attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine.
measures: Measures bilirubin, a yellowish substance from the normal breakdown of old red blood cells. It helps check liver health, find the cause of jaundice and see whether a treatment is working.
low: A low bilirubin is usually not a concern and may be caused by antibiotics, birth control pills, sleeping pills or seizure medicines.
high: A high bilirubin may be caused by hemolytic anemia, liver disease or a blockage in the bile ducts.
notes: Normal ranges vary by laboratory and sex. Some medicines, certain foods and strenuous exercise can raise it, and bilirubin is only one measure of liver health.
